questions.question: What happens if the tenant abandons the apartment?
questions.expected: Landlord may retake possession and relet; tenant stays liable for rent until the unit is relet, if the landlord makes good-faith efforts.
questions.answer:
If the tenant abandons the apartment, the Landlord has the right to retake possession of the Premises in accordance with applicable law and proceed to relet the Premises to mitigate damages. The Tenant remains liable for the rent due under the remaining term of the Lease until the Premises are relet, provided the Landlord makes reasonable, good-faith efforts to find a new tenant.

The Tenant's personal property left behind upon vacating or abandoning the Premises shall be handled by the Landlord in accordance with New York state law. The Landlord shall provide the Tenant with reasonable notice to retrieve such property before disposing of it. The Tenant shall be responsible for any costs incurred by the Landlord in storing or disposing of such items.

The Security Deposit is held as security for the faithful performance of the Tenant's obligations. If the Tenant vacates the Premises with unpaid rent, the Landlord shall be entitled to apply the Security Deposit toward the satisfaction of such unpaid rent and any other damages, as permitted by law, following the required itemized notice.

The Tenant's security deposit shall be returned to the Tenant, less any deductions for unpaid rent or damages beyond reasonable wear and tear, within fourteen (14) days after the Tenant vacates the Premises.
